narrative:
Short impact summary

Smart Cities (2024), published by Springer Nature, has been cited 22 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 10% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it has been downloaded 4,816 times and is used in teaching.

Full narrative

Smart Cities by Fateh Belaïd and Anvita Arora was published by Springer Nature in 2024. It is part of the Studies in energy, resource and environmental economics series. Conceptually, the work connects to Computer science.

OpenAlex records 22 citations. That places it in the top 10% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2024 with 11 citing works. Notable citing venues include Sustainability, Smart Cities and Contributions to economics. The citing works include 16 journal articles and 5 book chapters. They come from 24 countries, led by Saudi Arabia, Poland and Australia.

In teaching, it is discussed in 3 recorded lectures. It has been downloaded 4,816 times via OAPEN. It is recorded in 2 library collections.
narrative_llm:
Short impact summary

Smart Cities (2024) by Fateh Belaïd and Anvita Arora is showing early but meaningful scholarly traction: it is already in the top 10% of cited works for its field and year, with 22 OpenAlex citations, alongside 4,816 recorded downloads. The record also shows pedagogical reach, with three YouTube videos discussing the book, suggesting it is being used as a reference point beyond the immediate research literature.

Full narrative

Smart Cities has quickly established itself as a visible contribution to the smart-city and urban sustainability conversation. The book’s citation performance is notable for a 2024 publication: its 22 OpenAlex citations place it in the top 10% of works in its field and year, indicating that it is being taken up at a strong pace relative to contemporaneous output. The citing literature is concentrated in articles and book chapters, which is typical of a book that is being used to inform subsequent research rather than only being read in isolation.

The shape of the citation record suggests a broad interdisciplinary audience. Most citing works are clustered around smart cities, mobility, transport, and urban infrastructure, with additional attention to energy, environment, and economic growth. That pattern aligns closely with the book’s own focus on the socioeconomic, environmental, and policy implications of smart cities, and it indicates that readers are using it as a source for both conceptual framing and applied urban analysis. Citations appear across a range of venues and countries, with especially visible uptake in education-linked research communities.

Usage evidence strengthens the picture of reach. The book has 4,816 downloads in OAPEN, showing sustained reading interest for an open-access volume. The repository record also indicates open availability through multiple open instances, which likely supports discoverability and access. In addition, the teaching-adoption signals point to classroom and public-facing engagement: three YouTube videos discuss the book, supporting its role as a pedagogical anchor for explaining smart-city themes to broader audiences.

At the same time, the evidence base is still early and somewhat uneven. There is no event-data record in the digest, so the public-discourse picture cannot be reconstructed from this source set. Even so, the combination of strong early citation uptake, substantial download activity, and repeated discussion in video formats shows that Smart Cities is already functioning as both a scholarly reference and a teaching resource in the evolving smart-city literature.
